text:
max: quick thread — did an experiment with bandwidth-aware micro-lanes + a small prefetch budget, results look promising but odd at 95th pct. TL;DR: small tenants got better p50, big tenants saw some 95th spikes.

priya: can you paste the config you used? was this on dedicated or hosted pool?

max: hosted pool, pilot cluster n4-gpu-2. config snippet below:
```
batcher: 
  lanes: [micro, shared]
  micro_lane_budget_tokens: 128
  prefetch_budget_ratio: 0.1
  bandwidth_weight: {micro: 0.8, shared: 0.2}
  eviction_policy: damped_hysteresis
```

dan: hmm the prefetch_budget_ratio looks low for long-context requests. did you enable kv-cache pinning?

max: kv pinning ON, but we kept prefetch conservative to avoid cold-start penalties for the shared lane.

lia: 95th spike could be from oversized micro-batches starving KV warmup for heavy tenants. Micro-lanes prioritizing bandwidth means small requests go fast but large ones wait and then blow up when they finally run.

kevin: agree. We saw similar in the spillway experiment — need headroom tokens reserved for long-running requests. Suggest adding a lease token pool per-tenant that the scheduler can dip into for warmup.

priya: OTOH, lease pool complicates fairness accounting. How do we charge/cap it? Per-minute tokens? per-request capped amount?

max: proposal: per-tenant warmup tokens = min( max(ceil(avg_seq_len/64)*64, 128), 1024 ) with refill tied to recent throughput. That keeps cost bounded.

sara: also watch admission boundary: is admission deciding lane or coalescer? If admission assigns lane then coalescer sees already-separated traffic and can't rebalance. We should keep lane assignment late to allow coalescer to merge when load is low.

dan: good call. Late-binding lane assignment + a short deferral window (5-10ms) for coalescer to form better batches could smooth 95th. But micro-lane SLA for tiny requests needs a fastpath that skips deferral.

lia: can we add a fastpath flag on requests under X tokens so they bypass deferral? then lane decision path: if fastpath -> micro; else -> defer for coalesce window -> choose lane based on backlog + bandwidth score.

kevin: must also update telemetry: track lane_switches, warmup_tokens_consumed, deferral_hits, and per-tenant 95/50 delta. Without that we won't know if new heuristics are helping.

max: action items: 1) I’ll run another sweep with warmup token pool (128–512) + late-binding deferral 8ms. 2) priya/help run a dedicated cluster test to rule out host-level IO noise. 3) kevin/obs add metrics (lane_switches, warmup_tokens). 4) dan/lia prototype fastpath bypass.

priya: noted — will schedule dedicated run tomorrow AM. tagging @buildbot for a canary deploy after prototypes land. :rocket:

buildbot: deploy request queued: canary-batcher/experiment-4023456789 -> env:staging, ETA ~ 45m. Logs will post in #eng-runtime when done.

kevin: small nit — document the charging model for warmup tokens in the batcher RBAC docs so sales/sre can answer billing questions if customers notice cost change.

max: yes, I'll draft a short doc and attach to the RFC follow-up. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sara: also add a rollback flag in the runtime so we can flip back to global-queueing instantly if spikes worsen. keep safe.

max: agreed. will include rollback and a canary run plan in the follow-up.

lia: love the approach — feels like a middle ground between pure micro-lanes and global queueing. looking forward to measurements.

max: end of thread — will post results here after the canary.
